title: Plant Water Relation
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET / NEET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Properties of Water & Root Hair Anatomy
points: Water as life medium: Universal solvent, high specific heat, high heat of vaporization, high cohesive and adhesive forces (high tensile strength), neutral pH, thermal stability.
Root absorption zones: Root cap (protective) → Meristematic zone (cell division) → Elongation zone (expansion) → Root Hair zone / Maturation zone (specialized zone of water absorption).
Root hair structure: Unicellular, unbranched, tubular extension of epiblema (piliferous layer); contains large central vacuole surrounded by thin peripheral cytoplasm.
Root hair cell wall layers: Double layered. Outer pectic layer (hydrophilic, highly permeable, retains water like sponge); Inner cellulosic layer (structural, semi-permeable).

formulas.label: Root hair cell wall composition
formulas.expr: Outer layer: Pectin (hydrophilic, water-retaining) | Inner layer: Cellulose (structural)

formulas.label: Root absorption zone hierarchy
formulas.expr: Root cap → Meristematic zone → Elongation zone → Root Hair / Maturation zone (water absorption)

nodes.title: Water Absorption Mechanisms: Imbibition, Diffusion & Osmosis
points: Imbibition: Adsorption of water by hydrophilic colloids without forming solution (substances: proteins > pectin > starch > cellulose). Generates enormous Imbibition Pressure (IP); drives seed germination and rock splitting.
Diffusion: Movement of particles from higher chemical potential / diffusion pressure to lower along concentration gradient. Diffusion Pressure Deficit (DPD) / Suction Pressure (SP).
Osmosis: Special diffusion of solvent (water) across semipermeable membrane into a region of higher solute concentration.

DPD Classical Formula: DPD = OP − TP (where OP = Osmotic Pressure, TP = Turgor Pressure). In flaccid cell (TP = 0): DPD = OP; In fully turgid cell (TP = OP): DPD = 0; In plasmolysed cell (TP negative): DPD = OP + TP.
Water flow direction: Water always moves from Lower DPD → Higher DPD!

formulas.label: Diffusion Pressure Deficit (DPD) classical formula
formulas.expr: DPD = OP − TP (where OP = Osmotic Pressure, TP = Turgor Pressure)

formulas.label: DPD conditions table
formulas.expr: Flaccid cell: DPD = OP | Turgid cell: DPD = 0 | Plasmolysed cell: DPD = OP − (−TP) = OP + TP

formulas.label: Direction of water flow (DPD)
formulas.expr: Water flows from Lower DPD → Higher DPD

nodes.title: Water Potential (Ψ_w) & Thermodynamic Principles
points: Water potential (Ψ_w): Measure of free energy of water per unit volume; expressed in bars or MegaPascals (MPa).
Reference standard: Water potential of pure water at atmospheric pressure and standard temperature is ZERO (Ψ_w = 0, maximum possible value).
Solute potential / Osmotic potential (Ψ_s): Decrease in water potential caused by dissolved solutes. Always NEGATIVE. Greater the solute concentration, more negative the Ψ_s.
Pressure potential (Ψ_p): Hydrostatic pressure developed in cell; positive in turgid cells (equivalent to turgor pressure), can be negative in xylem under tension.
Water Potential Equation: Ψ_w = Ψ_s + Ψ_p. Water always moves spontaneously from Higher Ψ_w (less negative) → Lower Ψ_w (more negative).

formulas.label: Water Potential fundamental equation
formulas.expr: Ψ_w = Ψ_s + Ψ_p (where Ψ_s = solute potential, Ψ_p = pressure potential)

formulas.label: Pure water standard potential
formulas.expr: Ψ_w(pure water at 1 atm, 25 °C) = 0 bar / MPa (maximum possible value)

formulas.label: Direction of water flow (Potential)
formulas.expr: Water moves from Higher Ψ_w (less negative) → Lower Ψ_w (more negative)

nodes.title: Plasmolysis, Deplasmolysis & Solution Tonicity
points: Tonicity classification: 1) Hypotonic solution: Lower solute concentration than cell sap → Endosmosis → Cell becomes turgid; 2) Isotonic solution: Equal concentration → No net movement → Cell flaccid; 3) Hypertonic solution: Higher concentration than cell sap → Exosmosis → Plasmolysis.
Plasmolysis: Shrinkage of protoplast away from cell wall when plant cell is placed in hypertonic solution due to exosmosis.
Stages of plasmolysis: 1) Limiting plasmolysis (TP becomes zero); 2) Incipient plasmolysis (protoplast pulls away at cell corners); 3) Complete plasmolysis (protoplast rounds off in center).
Crucial feature: The space between the shrunken protoplast and the cell wall in a plasmolysed cell is occupied by the EXTERNAL HYPERTONIC SOLUTION!
Deplasmolysis: Reversible phenomenon where plasmolysed cell placed in hypotonic solution or pure water absorbs water by endosmosis, regaining turgidity.

formulas.label: Solution tonicity effects
formulas.expr: Hypotonic = Endosmosis (Turgid) | Hypertonic = Exosmosis (Plasmolysis) | Isotonic = No net movement (Flaccid)

formulas.label: Fluid occupying space in plasmolysed cell
formulas.expr: Space between cell wall and shrunken protoplast = Hypertonic external solution

nodes.title: Pathways of Water Movement in Roots: Apoplast vs Symplast
points: Path of absorbed water: Root hair → Epiblema → Cortex → Endodermis → Pericycle → Protoxylem vessels.
1. Apoplast Pathway: Non-living pathway through porous cell walls and intercellular spaces via capillarity and bulk flow. Fast, offers minimal resistance, non-selective.
2. Symplast Pathway: Living pathway through cytoplasm of adjacent cells interconnected by Plasmodesmata. Slower, regulated across cell membranes.
3. Vacuolar Pathway: Osmotic movement from vacuole to vacuole across tonoplasts.

Casparian Strip Checkpoint: Endodermal cells have tangential and radial walls impregnated with suberin forming impermeable Casparian Strips. Apoplastic water is strictly blocked and forced into the symplast pathway to enter xylem!

formulas.label: Root water pathway sequence
formulas.expr: Root hair → Epiblema → Cortex → Endodermis (Casparian strip) → Pericycle → Xylem

formulas.label: Apoplast vs Symplast comparison
formulas.expr: Apoplast: Cell walls & spaces (non-living, fast) | Symplast: Cytoplasm via Plasmodesmata (living, regulated)

nodes.title: Ascent of Sap: Root Pressure & Transpiration Pull Theory
points: Ascent of Sap: Upward translocation of water and dissolved minerals from roots to uppermost leaves against gravity.

1. Root Pressure Theory (Joseph Priestley): Active metabolic pumping of ions into root xylem creates positive hydrostatic pressure (+1 to +2 bars). Explains Guttation (exudation of liquid water droplets via Hydathodes at vein endings during night/early morning). Insufficient for tall trees (>100 m).
2. Cohesion-Tension / Transpiration Pull Theory (Dixon & Joly, 1894 - Universally Accepted):
- Cohesion: Strong mutual intermolecular attraction between water molecules (tensile strength up to 350 atm).
- Adhesion: Attraction between polar water molecules and hydrophilic lignified xylem vessel walls.
- Transpiration Pull: Rapid evaporation of water from stomata creates massive negative hydrostatic suction tension in xylem conduit, pulling continuous unbroken water column upwards.

formulas.label: Dixon & Joly Cohesion-Tension triad
formulas.expr: Cohesion (H₂O-H₂O attraction) + Adhesion (H₂O-xylem wall) + Transpiration Pull (negative suction tension)

formulas.label: Guttation vs Transpiration
formulas.expr: Guttation: Liquid water via Hydathodes (Root pressure, night/dawn) | Transpiration: Water vapor via Stomata (Pull, daytime)

nodes.title: Transpiration: Mechanism & Stomatal Regulation
points: Transpiration types: Stomatal (90-93% of total loss), Cuticular (3-9%), Lenticular (0.1%).

Stomatal apparatus: Stomatal pore flanked by 2 Guard cells (kidney-shaped in dicots; dumbbell-shaped in grasses/monocots) surrounded by subsidiary cells. Guard cells have thick, inelastic inner walls and thin, elastic outer walls with radial cellulose microfibrils.

Levitt's Active K⁺ Transport Theory (Opening in Light): Light stimulates PEP carboxylase → Malic acid dissociates into Malate²⁻ + 2H⁺. Protons (H⁺) actively pumped out of guard cells into subsidiary cells in exchange for K⁺ ions. Cl⁻ co-enters. Accumulation of K⁺ malate lowers Ψ_w of guard cells → Endosmosis → Turgor pressure rises → Outer thin walls bulge out, pulling inner thick walls apart → Stoma OPENS.
Closing in Darkness / Water Stress: Abscisic acid (ABA) promotes rapid K⁺ and Cl⁻ efflux → Water exits → Guard cells become flaccid → Stoma CLOSES.

formulas.label: Stomatal opening active ion exchange
formulas.expr: Guard cells: H⁺ pumped OUT → K⁺ and Cl⁻ pumped IN → Ψ_w drops → Endosmosis → Turgid → Stoma Opens

formulas.label: Stomatal closing trigger (Stress)
formulas.expr: Water deficit → Abscisic Acid (ABA) release → K⁺ efflux → Flaccid guard cells → Stoma Closes

nodes.title: Translocation of Photosynthates: Mass Flow Hypothesis
points: Source-Sink relationship: Source (organ photosynthesizing or mobilizing sugars e.g. mature green leaves, storage tubers in spring); Sink (organ consuming or storing sugars e.g. roots, fruits, growing shoot tips). Direction of phloem transport is Multidirectional / Bidirectional.
Münch Pressure Flow / Mass Flow Hypothesis (1930):
1. Phloem Loading: Sucrose actively transported from mesophyll into companion cells and sieve tube elements using ATP.
2. Osmotic Gradient: High sucrose lowers water potential (Ψ_w) of sieve tube → Water enters from adjacent xylem by osmosis, developing high turgor pressure.
3. Mass Flow: High turgor pressure forces bulk flow of sugar solution through phloem sieve plates towards sink.
4. Phloem Unloading: Sucrose actively transported out at sink cells; water potential rises, water returns to xylem.

formulas.label: Phloem loading osmotic pressure cascade
formulas.expr: Active loading of Sucrose → Lowers Ψ_w in Sieve tube → H₂O enters from Xylem → High Turgor Pressure → Mass Flow to Sink

formulas.label: Xylem vs Phloem transport contrast
formulas.expr: Xylem: Unidirectional (Root → Leaf, negative tension) | Phloem: Multidirectional (Source ↔ Sink, positive pressure)

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Experiments
points: Board Q1: Explain Dixon and Joly's Cohesion-Tension theory for ascent of sap.
Board Q2: Describe Levitt's active K⁺ transport theory for stomatal opening and closing with reactions.
Board Q3: Explain why Casparian strips in the endodermis force water into the symplastic pathway.
Board Q4: Distinguish between Transpiration and Guttation (vapor vs liquid drops, stomata vs hydathodes, pure water vs solute-rich).

Ringing / Girdling Experiment (Malpighi): Removal of a ring of bark (phloem) up to xylem level causes swelling above the girdle due to accumulation of photosynthates, while roots starve, proving phloem transports organic food.

formulas.label: Girdling experiment outcome
formulas.expr: Bark (phloem) removed → Sugars accumulate ABOVE ring (swelling) | Roots starve first (proves phloem translocates food)

formulas.label: Potometer bubble rate formula
formulas.expr: Rate of transpiration = Volume of water absorbed / Time = (πr² × distance moved by air bubble) / t

nodes.title: MHT-CET & NEET High-Speed Shortcuts & Traps
points: TRAP 1: Water potential sign: Pure water Ψ_w = 0 (MAXIMUM). Addition of solute ALWAYS makes Ψ_w negative. Water moves from HIGHER Ψ_w (e.g. −2 bar) to LOWER Ψ_w (e.g. −10 bar).
TRAP 2: DPD vs Water Potential: DPD is numerically equal to Ψ_w with OPPOSITE sign! DPD = 10 bar ⇔ Ψ_w = −10 bar. Water flows from LOW DPD to HIGH DPD, but HIGH Ψ_w to LOW Ψ_w!
TRAP 3: Fully turgid cell: TP = OP ⇒ DPD = 0; Ψ_p = −Ψ_s ⇒ Ψ_w = 0.
TRAP 4: Guard cell shape: Dicots = Kidney-shaped / Reniform; Monocots / Grasses (Poaceae) = Dumbbell-shaped!
TRAP 5: Guttation fluid: Guttation water is NOT pure water; it contains dissolved minerals, amino acids, and organic acids, exuded through hydathodes.

formulas.label: DPD to Water Potential conversion
formulas.expr: Ψ_w = −DPD (e.g. DPD = 6 atm → Ψ_w = −6 atm)

formulas.label: Water flow direction comparison rule
formulas.expr: Water flows: Low DPD → High DPD | High Ψ_w → Low Ψ_w | Hypotonic → Hypertonic

formulas.label: Guard cell morphology exception
formulas.expr: Dicots = Bean / Kidney shaped | Grasses / Monocots = Dumbbell shaped
